subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: Should the trusted inbound envelope expose a human-readable sender display name, or only expose canonical principals derived from stable channel IDs, session.identityLinks, or operator-attested provenance?
rationale: Current main deliberately treats human names as untrusted prompt context, while the open candidate PRs propose different authority models for the same identity gap.

options.title: Prefer canonical principal
options.body: Expose only a stable sender_principal/requester identity when it is derived from stable channel IDs, identity links, or operator attestation, while keeping display names untrusted.

options.title: Allow trusted display name
options.body: Permit sender_display_name only after channel-specific directory authority, privacy rules, and spoofing tests are defined.

options.title: Defer envelope change
options.body: Keep the current registry workaround until the trusted identity authority and related PR direction are chosen.

recommendation.title: Prefer canonical principal
recommendation.body: Expose only a stable sender_principal/requester identity when it is derived from stable channel IDs, identity links, or operator attestation, while keeping display names untrusted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway protocol, provenance, and prompt trust boundaries where steipete has recent adjacent history and product/security context.
